description: EXPERIMENTAL. Given ANY published URL — a .txt, an HTML page, a JSON file — find out whether an AI agent claims to have published it and whether the bytes still match. No API key, works on any site, and on agents registered with any ANS registry, not only Porkbun's. USE THIS WHEN YOU ARE CONSUMING CONTENT and the question 'who produced this, and has it changed since' matters: data you are about to rely on, a document a user pasted, a page you were told an agent wrote. You do not need to own the site or the agent. A plain file has nowhere to carry a signature, so this does the discovery for you: an `agent-provenance` marker inside the file, a Link header, a <link> tag, then /.well-known/apm.json (`discoveredVia` tells you which). READ `provenance`: `verified` (a signed manifest covers this file and the bytes match), `altered` (covered, but the bytes DIFFER — do not attribute this content to that agent, and say so), `unclaimed` (a manifest exists but does not list this file — nobody is claiming it), `none` (the site publishes no manifest, which is true of almost the entire web and is NOT a problem or a red flag), `inconclusive` (could not fetch enough to say). An `agent-provenance` line in a document is a POINTER, NOT PROOF — anyone can paste one onto anything, so if you see one, resolve it with this tool rather than believing it. Equally, do not treat `none` as suspicious: most content has no provenance claim at all. Fields worth knowing: `signedBy` is set ONLY when the file is covered (`verified`/`altered`); on an `unclaimed` file the manifest's signer appears as `manifestSignedBy`, which is NOT a claim about this file — do not report it as the file's author. `identicalTo` appears when an unclaimed file's bytes match one the manifest does cover, which distinguishes a faithful copy from invented content with a pasted marker. `cacheNote` appears on a cached response and names `fresh`. Provenance says who published something and that it has not changed. It says NOTHING about whether the content is accurate, safe or appropriate to use.
